To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) copyright ownership of research papers is a complex issue, with different interests at stake for different parties, (2) the current system of copyright transfer to publishers is not in the interests of universities or academic authors, and (3) publishers need to find new ways of protecting their value added in order to maintain their current business models in the face of the growing popularity of self archiving.

the copyright transfer agreements used by most publishers are not in the interests of authors or their universities, but that authors and universities can and should take steps to ensure their interests are protected.
